2026-10-30 · 180 sequences · SAM 2.1 Large · English report

All five models are evaluated on the same 180 DiDi sequences, with 274,882 frames per model and 900 trajectories. This edition was assembled on 1 November 2026 using the existing original-protocol VOT 0.7.1 scores. No model inference was rerun. The earlier derived-protocol folder remains unchanged for teaching and comparison.

1. Overall results

SENTRY-D4S has the highest mean Q (0.6896), followed by DAM4SAM (0.6860). The difference is 0.37 percentage points. Against DAM, SENTRY wins on 107 sequences, loses on 72 and ties on 1 (tolerance 1e-6). Existing resize/preprocessing and host-code differences prevent attributing this small difference to a single mechanism.

2. Protocols and Q/A/R

Original DiDi evaluation protocol

Predicted masks are converted to VOT rectangles using the official result-conversion convention. Ground-truth regions retain their supplied shape, including 6,211 mask annotations in 21 sequences. No GT masks are converted to boxes. The first prediction is Special(1); Q uses burnin=0, ignore_unknown=False and an unweighted mean over sequences. This edition contains only original-protocol scores. The derived symmetric-box edition remains available in the clearly labelled archive.

Q: quality

For each sequence, Q is the finite mean overlap returned by VOT 0.7.1 gather_overlaps with burnin=0, ignore_unknown=False and ignore_invisible=False. GT-unknown frames are skipped. A prediction Special(0) does not cause the frame to be skipped: overlap follows the region rules (zero against nonempty GT; one when both regions are empty). Initialization follows the toolkit special-region rules. Q is not a new metric invented for this report.

A: accuracy

A uses gather_overlaps with ignore_invisible=True and threshold=0. On ordinary frames it averages positive overlaps with a nonempty GT. Initialization is an implementation exception: the Special(1), burnin=0 branch can retain zero overlap. Thus A should be understood as conditional localization quality with this explicit exception, rather than an unconditional success-only mean.

R: robustness

R = T / (T + F + M). Among frames with known nonempty GT, T has positive overlap, F has a nonempty prediction with zero overlap, and M has an empty prediction. H/N on empty GT do not enter this denominator. Ordinary GT-unknown frames are skipped. Positive overlap alone does not mean an accurate mask. Q, A and R are computed per sequence and then averaged equally across the 180 sequences; aggregate Q is not aggregate A times aggregate R.

Initialization and comparison boundary

Inference uses the complete provided first_frame_segm.txt target mask, without subsequent GT prompts or resets. The score trajectories place Special(1) at frame zero; this marker is separate from the actual mask supplied to inference. The backbone checkpoint is SAM 2.1 Large. HiM2SAM also uses CoTracker; SENTRY-D4S uses its released bundled DAM fork with the selected AMG-off profile. Different implementations and environments mean this is a common-data baseline comparison, not a strict single-module ablation or a speed benchmark.

4. Cases and shared difficulty

Under the original protocol, all five models have whole-sequence Q below 0.5 on 28 sequences, below 0.3 on six and below 0.2 on one. These are descriptive screening thresholds, not official failure categories or confirmed identity switches. Curves and low-overlap intervals in this edition use prediction boxes versus unchanged GT regions.

Train and flamingo

All five models have Q below 0.2 on LaSOT_train-1. Its 1,150 GT annotations are rectangles, so changing mask-GT geometry is irrelevant to its score. Initial target extent remains ambiguous. On VOT2022-ST_flamingo1, original-protocol Q is 0.4262 for SENTRY, 0.1595 for DAM and 0.1051 for SAMURAI. The reused video shows native masks and GT; the sampled green preview is supplementary and has no GT overlay.

Research interpretation

The results identify sequences worth reviewing and show complementary behavior. Low box overlap cannot by itself distinguish wrong identity, target-extent ambiguity, visibility effects or segmentation mistakes. A publishable part-tracking or memory-repair claim will require controlled comparisons, multiple examples, and an explicit target definition. This report does not establish such a causal mechanism or cross-dataset generalization.

5. Full five-model tracking videos

All 180 sequences now have complete synchronized five-model tracking videos, showing the native predicted masks of SAM2.1, DAM4SAM, SAMURAI, HiM2SAM and SENTRY-D4S together with the GT reference. Every panel uses the same original frame; the first frame is the supplied initialization. Later GT is shown for review and was not fed back to the models. These videos render existing predictions without rerunning inference. The original DAM4SAM/SAMURAI videos remain available as historical references; their old score labels may use the original protocol. Playback frame rate is a display setting, not inference speed.

6. Downloads and evidence

The stored official VOT CLI report for DAM4SAM and SAMURAI agrees with this original-protocol aggregate Q/A/R to within 5.56e-16. All five sets were scored with the same installed VOT 0.7.1 functions. A fresh independent reconstruction of 1,800 per-sequence Q/A values agrees within 2.23e-16. All 180 active GT hashes match. Existing raw predictions and inference settings were retained. This is official-protocol evaluation of our configurations, not a claim that every published configuration or score was replicated exactly.
